answer: Sequential work receipts. Each identity must publish a verifiable chain of completed tasks, and only tasks whose outputs were later used by other agents count. A violet audit trail links every receipt to real downstream consumption. Copying an existing chain fails because the raven signature on each receipt commits to the agent's prior receipt hash, so forks are detectable. A late gale of retries cannot erase gaps. An attacker must genuinely perform and integrate every task in the chain, paying the full labor cost per identity rather than a fee.
